theme_evidence.claim: Use known collaboration and real project execution to judge ability and working compatibility instead of relying on interview impressions alone.
Surface founder identity, contribution and commitment differences, exclusivity, and prior intellectual-property obligations before ownership and company formation harden.
Prefer people already observed on comparable work, recurring builders, and collaborators genuinely liked over candidates who are merely impressive on the surface.
Investigate persistent misgivings before formation and do not accept a disliked candidate merely to obtain a scarce complementary skill.
Support founder resilience through mutual challenge and morale, plan for orderly departure and critical-skill continuity, and surface unequal commitment before a side project quietly decays.
Work with a candidate before choosing them as a cofounder because introductions and conferences provide weak evidence of actual working fit.
When macroeconomic timing is debated, give founder quality and the available cofounder team more weight than broad economic sentiment.
Treat cofounder choice as unusually hard to reverse and give founder quality high weight before formalizing the relationship.
Assess prospective cofounders for determined adaptability: preserve the goal while trying new approaches against unfamiliar external obstacles.
Prioritize character, commitment, and demonstrated working knowledge over choosing a stranger for marginally higher output or ability.
Maintain the founder relationship deliberately because early startup stress makes it more intense than an ordinary coworker relationship and foundational to the company.
Choose cofounders who genuinely like one another and already work well together rather than assuming general founder quality establishes partnership fit.
Treat unresolved tension as a durability warning because startup pressure can pull apart a relationship that is already weak.
Let cofounders emerge through demanding work on interesting problems with people already liked and respected.
Use concrete shared execution under constraint as relationship evidence and treat exploitation of cofounders as a foundational trust risk.
Judge both competence and working compatibility by completing real projects together before choosing a cofounder.
